title: My Son-In-Law Forged The Deed, Sold My Building, And Left Me $5,200. So I Voided The Sale
description: I retired after 27 years as a mail carrier and used my late husband's $143,000 life insurance to buy a six-unit building with my son-in-law. He forged a quitclaim deed, sold the building to a developer for $910,000, and left me a $5,200 vacancy check, but the original co-ownership agreement was still hidden in my fireproof lockbox. I voided the sale and now he unclogs drains at Unit of Deceit Rentals while every lease prints his deed fraud docket. #RevengeStory #FamilyBetrayal #DeedFraud
thumb_text: HE SOLD MY BUILDING. NOW HE DRAINS MY TRUST.
pinned_comment: I voided the sale and put him in a Drained My Trust coverall, but what would you have done if your son-in-law forged the deed, sold your building for $910,000, and left you a $5,200 vacancy check? If you have survived a family deed fraud like this, share your story in the comments.
